verdicts.evidence: On semi-SUPPORT (coupled by construction via shared factor h2), SALaD vs baseline gives ΔC-index = −0.0019 (SALaD better in only 1/5 paired seeds), ΔIBS = 0.0000, ΔMAE-Hinge = +0.04 — a statistical tie, not an improvement. On real SUPPORT, SALaD loses on all 5 paired splits (ΔC = −0.0052, 0/5 seeds). Independent seeds 100–102 reportedly show the same pattern.

The claim specifies 'consistent gains on 10 datasets,' but the logbook only tests 2 datasets (SUPPORT, semi-SUPPORT) with 1 survival layer (N-MTLR) out of 4. On those 2 datasets SALaD shows no gains over baseline, but the reduced scope (2/10 datasets, 1/4 layers) cannot confirm or fully refute the 10-dataset consistency claim, and the 'four disjoint factor categories' aspect is not directly evaluated.

overall: The logbook runs the authors' own SALaD code verbatim on real SUPPORT data and a semi-synthetic coupled dataset with a proper paired-seed protocol, finding that SALaD does not beat the plain baseline in the coupled regime (tie) and loses on real SUPPORT. The scope is limited to 1 of 4 survival layers and 2 of 10 datasets, so it falsifies the coupled-regime improvement claim for the tested slice but cannot fully assess the broader 10-dataset consistency claim.
